title: He Poisoned His Own Team Before Walking Into a Forbidden Lab . . . (Part 6)
credit: Swordmaster's Youngest Son (Hwangze Penguin / Mr. Big / AZI)

segments.say: A monster with a human face looks up at Jin, begs him to *kill* it, and Jin does.
To see how it got here, go back to an orc forest, where Jin's dragon is secretly *babysitting* his classmates.
Jin asked Murakhan to keep the cadets alive, so a cat in the bushes tells the orc pack to *scatter*.
The orcs panic and run. Murakhan trots off muttering that Jin will pay him in *comic books*.
Then the cat freezes. Something huge is *coming* through the forest, and it's not an orc.
One cadet sits alone and feels the sky go dark. Is it going to *rain*? Nope.
Out of the dark steps a Tomb Giant, a stone knight built to guard the tombs of the *gods*.
Murakhan stops hiding. He turns into a huge black *dragon* wrapped in blue fire.
He says his kind wiped these giants out two thousand years ago, so what is one doing *here*?
The giant doesn't answer. It charges, and the dragon opens his jaws and blows it to *pieces*.
Next morning Murakhan, back in human form, is *wrecked*.
He suspects the Zeifls are behind this, and he decides not to tell Jin, because the kid would go *hunting*.
Meanwhile a man named Bubarre cries over his masterpiece, the Tomb Giant, which somebody just *destroyed*.
Bishkel, vice chief of the Kinzelo Revolutionaries, tells him it was a dragon. Not just any dragon, the Dragon of *Shadows*.
Bishkel's answer is to set up a meeting with the *Zeifls*.
Back at the academy, Jin walks in alive from lawless Mahmeet, and his *uncle* is thrilled.
He laughs that Jin hit the flagbearers who sent him there, and it's sure to *annoy* them.
In the yard, lowborn cadets whisper that Jin is only a four-star who gets all the *luck*.
Their leader Kazine Romero wants somebody to do something about it. Somebody turns around. It's *Jin*.
Jin asks how Kazine's arm is. Kazine thanks him for chopping it off so *cleanly*, because it made reattaching easier.
Kazine says Jin only has to say the word to get him *whipped*. Jin says he'd never. Kazine says he's being insolent on purpose.
Jin points out that Kazine is a five-star, one of the best cadets in the class, so why talk behind his *back*?
Then he lifts his sword and says don't go easy, go *all-out*. Main-character energy, honestly.
Kazine says you'll regret it and swings with everything he's got. That was *his* first mistake.
Steel clashes, but Jin can see every move. He has seen this swing *before*.
Kazine's last trick is an aura attack that kills any four-star knight, and Jin takes it *head-on*.
Jin was a five-star the whole time. At fifteen. He only fights when he knows he can *win*.
The word spreads fast. Two cadets stare across the hall and ask if Jin really beat *Kazine*. No way.
Kazine's boss isn't buying it either. She asks if he was *bribed* to lose, and he swears he'd never.
Everyone in the hall saw that aura. Jin has shown the whole clan his *teeth*, so she sends some of her own people along on his next *mission*.
At home Jin tells Gilly he did it on purpose, because the news will make his siblings *nervous*.
Only the first patriarch, his father and Luna ever hit five-star at fifteen. Jin is now *that* guy.
Murakhan the cat takes one look at him and asks what happened to *humility*.
Gilly says visitors from all over the world will crowd the banquet, and Jin smiles. A crowd means they can't *touch* him.
Not so fast. A butler crashes in gasping, because the siblings sent Jin to Kollon, a Zeifl *territory*.
Their mother storms in, screaming how they could send their youngest brother into Zeifl land.
Luntia, Ran and Vuigo stand stiff while she asks if they *ever* do anything but plot their brother's death.
They say competition is the clan's way. She says none of them hit five-star at fifteen, so they're not worth her *attention*.
She puts Luntia on probation and takes a rare sword from Ran and Vuigo. *Brutal*.
Then she turns to Jin and asks if he wants the mission cancelled, or if this favor will just *boost* his ego.
Jin says he likes the mission his siblings gave him. A battle he can win is a battle he'll *take*.
Ran and Vuigo's swords are his if he completes it, so Jin leaves the room *smiling*.
Jin thanks them for their concern. Then he meets his team, three cadets who all belong to Miu and Anne's *faction*.
The goal is to sneak into Kollon's historic sites and steal four *relics*.
In his past life, Jin remembers, the Zeifls enslaved the Kollon people and used a mana *mirror* to manufacture sorcerers.
So he'll go in, take the relic from the third *warehouse*, and see what they are hiding.
The team stops to rest and eat. Jin passes around food, and every one of them *chews*.
One minute later they are swaying on their feet. Jin smiles, says it's *just* a sleeping drug, and goes in alone.
At the warehouse two guards chat about girls and drinks, until Jin drops from the shadows and *wrecks* them.
Two guards, no alarms, and a plain padlock. Jin pops it open and walks *in*.
Inside is a magic circle written in blood. It only opens for *human* blood, so he cuts a guard and uses *that*.
The circle lights up red, and it turns out the guard wasn't *human* anymore.
The two knocked-out guards swell into red-eyed giants with muscles on top of their muscles. *Damn*.
Jin goes for the head. They get right back up. He goes for the heart. They *regenerate*.
Jin smirks. These are biological golems, forbidden magic, and each one has a core in the head, the heart, or the *abdomen*.
He checks them one at a time. Head, nothing. Heart, nothing. Only the abdomen is *left*.
He shatters the first core, then slices through the second, and the red glow finally *dies*.
The last body is still alive, and it's crying. *Please. Kill me.*
Jin stabs through its core and says one word. *I will.*
Nobody would ever choose to become a golem, he says, and they get thrown away the second they change.
Somebody is turning people into monsters in that warehouse, and Jin still has to find the *relic* before it finds him.
